Prior unsupported tabletop handoffs left the thin coin ungraspable; do not repeat that macro unchanged. If one arm cannot reach both observed endpoints, test a supported bimanual handoff with explicit moves and grips: the giving hand keeps possession while the receiving hand approaches a distinct accessible part of the coin, closes and settles before the giving hand opens. Single-arm move/grip operations preserve the other arm's command; home opens BOTH grippers, so never use home while either should retain the coin. Lower-level move permits sideways orientations. Check jaw/body clearance and coin-plane rotation, not merely TCP coincidence. This is an unverified hypothesis, not a successful prior program.
